planting.note: Set out after last frost; self-branches into a tidy mound without pinching.

directions: Part of the Mirage series bred for a compact, self-branching, mounded habit that resists breaking in shipping and in the garden. Produces bold violet-purple flower spikes from early spring through autumn, drawing hummingbirds and butterflies. Thrives in heat with good drainage and benefits from a light monthly feeding during the bloom season. More compact than seed-grown autumn sage, making it well suited to containers and border edges.

planting.note: Set out after last frost in full sun; tolerates reflected heat from paving.

directions: A Mirage-series selection with saturated cherry-red flower spikes held above a dense, rounded mound of small aromatic leaves. Blooms continuously from early spring into autumn and is a reliable hummingbird and butterfly draw. Functions as a reseeding annual in colder climates but overwinters as a woody-based perennial in warm southern gardens. Needs sharp drainage and little supplemental water once established.

planting.note: Plant in full sun with excellent drainage; deadhead spent spikes to extend bloom.

directions: An unusually soft-colored Mirage-series sage, with creamy white, two-lipped flowers flushed pale peachy pink above green-to-maroon bracts. Forms a bushy, semi-evergreen mound of small fragrant leaves and blooms from summer into autumn. Pairs well with brighter perennials as a cooling accent and tolerates heat and drought once rooted in. Best performance comes with full sun and lean, well-drained soil.

planting.note: Set out after frost danger passes; feed monthly during the growing season for best repeat bloom.

directions: Carries rich deep-purple flower spikes over a tight, self-branching mound from early spring through autumn. Bred for a more uniform, compact habit than open-pollinated autumn sage seedlings, it ships and transplants cleanly without legginess. Heat tolerant and deer resistant, it is a steady hummingbird and butterfly magnet. Hardy as a woody perennial in warm climates and grown as a long-blooming annual farther north.

planting.note: Plant in full sun with sharp drainage; avoid soggy winter soil.

directions: A warm-toned Mirage-series sage with deep salmon flowers set off by a dark calyx, carried on a compact, mounded plant from spring into fall. The unusual coral-salmon shade stands apart from the more common reds and pinks of autumn sage. Heat and drought tolerant once established, it draws hummingbirds reliably through the long bloom season. Suits containers and border fronts where a smaller, tidy habit is wanted.

planting.note: Set out in spring; thrives in full to partial sun with good drainage.

directions: A dwarf, more floriferous sport in the lineage of the popular bicolor sage 'Hot Lips,' covered from spring to frost in brilliant lipstick-red and white two-toned flowers. Grows as an upright, compact mound well suited to small gardens, containers, and border edging where full-size autumn sages would sprawl too wide. Heat and drought tolerant once rooted in, it needs only moderate water and sharp drainage. A strong draw for hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies through a long warm-season bloom.
